key_insight: The paper reformulates phase-field fracture for composite shells as a certified, replaceable constitutive operator that resolves shell strain into orthogonal deformation channels with exact algebraic closure.
engineering_relevance: This enables fracture models for fibre-reinforced curved shells that can use either analytic or learned material laws while preserving plane-stress condensation, consistent tangents, and solver robustness.
method: Maps Green-Lagrange strain through the shell metric and Cholesky factor into four orthogonal invariants.
Splits energy into fibre, inter-fibre, and interaction channels with channel-wise degradation and exact tension-compression treatment.
Adds a three-tier certification protocol for algebraic validity, solver state, and admissible training data.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests on notched IM7/8552 shells show accurate behavior in thin and curved regimes, with fibre orientation controlling damage/load capacity and curvature causing through-thickness fracture asymmetry.
watch_item: The framework relies on admissible operator conditions and positive residual stiffness for regular plane-stress condensation, so learned or custom laws must be carefully certified before deployment.
paper_title: Mechanism-resolved phase-field fracture of composite shells with a certified admissible constitutive operator
